scheme_name: Bihar Shatabdi AIDS Pirit Kalyan Yojana
description:
Bihar Shatabdi AIDS Pirit Kalyan Yojana was launched by the Government of Bihar on December 1, 2019. 

This scheme was initiated on World AIDS Day to provide support and assistance to individuals living with HIV/AIDS in the state of Bihar. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to improve the quality of life of people affected by HIV/AIDS. 

The scheme aims to provide financial assistance and various welfare measures to ensure that individuals living with HIV/AIDS can lead a dignified life. 

The specific goals include reducing stigma and discrimination against people living with HIV/AIDS. 

Another goal is to ensure that individuals affected by HIV/AIDS have access to essential healthcare services. 

The scheme also aims to provide economic support to families affected by HIV/AIDS. 

Under this scheme, financial assistance of INR 1,000 per month is provided to individuals living with HIV/AIDS. 

This financial assistance is aimed at helping them meet their daily needs and medical expenses. 

Additionally, the scheme provides for the establishment of support groups for individuals living with HIV/AIDS. 

These support groups are designed to provide emotional and psychological support to individuals and their families. 

The eligibility criteria for the Bihar Shatabdi AIDS Pirit Kalyan Yojana include individuals who are residents of Bihar. 

Applicants must be diagnosed with HIV/AIDS by a recognized medical institution. 

There is no specific age limit for eligibility under this scheme. 

However, the applicant must be able to provide valid proof of their HIV/AIDS status. 

Income criteria are also considered, and preference is given to individuals from economically weaker sections of society. 

The application process for the scheme is straightforward. 

Interested individuals must visit the nearest health center or designated government office. 

They need to fill out an application form specifically designed for the scheme. 

The application form requires personal details such as name, address, age, and contact information. 

Applicants must also provide proof of their HIV/AIDS diagnosis. 

This can be done through a medical report from a recognized healthcare provider. 

Additionally, applicants must submit proof of residence in Bihar. 

Documents required for the application include a government-issued ID, medical report, and proof of residence. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the concerned authorities. 

The review process typically takes about 15 to 30 days. 

If approved, the financial assistance is disbursed directly to the bank account of the beneficiary. 

The disbursement of funds occurs on a monthly basis. 

The scheme also includes provisions for regular health check-ups for beneficiaries. 

These health check-ups are conducted at designated healthcare facilities across Bihar. 

The implementing authority for the Bihar Shatabdi AIDS Pirit Kalyan Yojana is the Bihar State AIDS Control Society. 

The society operates under the Department of Health and Family Welfare, Government of Bihar. 

Individuals can contact the Bihar State AIDS Control Society for more information. 

The contact number for the society is 0612-221-8000. 

The email address for inquiries is bihar.aidscontrol@gmail.com. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to combat the HIV/AIDS epidemic in Bihar. 

According to the National AIDS Control Organization, Bihar has a significant number of people living with HIV/AIDS. 

The state has been working to reduce the prevalence of HIV through various awareness and prevention programs. 

The Bihar Shatabdi AIDS Pirit Kalyan Yojana is a crucial step in providing support to those affected. 

The scheme also aims to promote awareness about HIV/AIDS in the community. 

This includes educating people about prevention methods and reducing stigma. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 10 crore for the implementation of this scheme in the first year. 

This budget is expected to cover the financial assistance and operational costs associated with the scheme. 

The scheme is expected to benefit thousands of individuals living with HIV/AIDS in Bihar. 

According to estimates, there are approximately 1.2 million people living with HIV/AIDS in Bihar. 

The Bihar Shatabdi AIDS Pirit Kalyan Yojana is expected to reach a significant portion of this population. 

The government is also working on improving access to antiretroviral therapy for beneficiaries. 

This therapy is essential for managing HIV and improving the quality of life for those affected. 

The scheme is part of the larger National AIDS Control Program. 

This program aims to achieve the goal of ending the AIDS epidemic as a public health threat by 2030. 

The Bihar government is committed to ensuring that individuals living with HIV/AIDS receive the necessary support. 

The scheme has been well received by the community and has garnered positive feedback. 

Beneficiaries have reported improvements in their quality of life due to the financial assistance provided. 

The establishment of support groups has also been beneficial in providing emotional support. 

The government continues to monitor the implementation of the scheme closely. 

Regular assessments are conducted to evaluate the impact of the scheme on the target population. 

The Bihar Shatabdi AIDS Pirit Kalyan Yojana represents a significant step towards addressing the needs of individuals living with HIV/AIDS in Bihar. 

It reflects the government's commitment to social welfare and public health. 

The scheme is expected to evolve over time based on the needs and feedback from beneficiaries. 

Overall, the Bihar Shatabdi AIDS Pirit Kalyan Yojana is a vital initiative aimed at improving the lives of those affected by HIV/AIDS in the state. 

It serves as a model for similar initiatives in other states across India. 

The government is hopeful that with continued support and awareness, the stigma associated with HIV/AIDS will diminish. 

This will lead to a more inclusive society where individuals living with HIV/AIDS can thrive.
